records.visible-1:
On 13 December 2021 at meeting S/PV.8926, the Security Council voted on draft S/2021/990, introduced by Ireland and Niger with other sponsors. It proposed making climate-related security risks a central part of United Nations conflict prevention. The vote was 12 in favour, two against and one abstention. India and Russia opposed it and China abstained. Russia's negative vote as a permanent member prevented adoption. The draft created no new Council authority or requirements.

Russia opposed the draft's automatic link between climate change and security, preferring substantive work through specialist forums like the UNFCCC. Instead, it advocated for an alternative draft addressing the Sahel's specific circumstances and multiple sources of insecurity.

It proposed making climate-related security risks a central part of United Nations conflict prevention. The vote was 12 in favour, two against and one abstention. India and Russia opposed it and China abstained. Russia's negative vote as a permanent member prevented adoption. The draft created no new Council authority or requirements.

records.visible-3:
On 13 December 2021 at meeting S/PV.8926, the Security Council voted on draft S/2021/990, introduced by Ireland and Niger with other sponsors. It proposed making climate-related security risks a central part of United Nations conflict prevention. The vote was 12 in favour, two against and one abstention. India and Russia opposed it and China abstained. Russia's negative vote as a permanent member prevented adoption. The draft created no new Council authority or requirements.

Russia opposed an automatic climate-security link, preferring substantive work at the UNFCCC and a draft focused on the Sahel. India opposed moving climate decisions to the Security Council, favoring a narrower alternative limited to the Sahel region. Both delegations supported a Sahel-specific alternative while rejecting a universal Security Council approach.

On 13 December 2021 at meeting S/PV.8926, the Security Council voted on draft S/2021/990, introduced by Ireland and Niger with other sponsors. It proposed making climate-related security risks a central part of United Nations conflict prevention. The vote was 12 in favour, two against and one abstention. India and Russia opposed it and China abstained. Russia's negative vote as a permanent member prevented adoption. The draft created no new Council authority or requirements.

China abstained to support country-specific Council consideration of climate risks in peace and security rather than treating climate change as a universal security challenge. It emphasized common but differentiated responsibilities, urging developed nations to fulfill financing, technology transfer, and capacity-building commitments.
